title: Customer snapshot: integrity choices & exec brief
body:
Draft customer communication packet — compact + evidence-first. Purpose: provide a short, executive-friendly status note for the public status page and a slightly longer customer-facing postmortem + a choice-driven recovery offer with a small self-audit kit customers can use to validate their data and opt into recovery modes. This is intended for enterprise tenants impacted by the degraded inference responses on 2026-05-09 02:14–03:40 UTC (INC-4521).

One-line status (for Status page banner):
- May 9 02:14–03:40 UTC: Service degradation impacting text generation and streaming responses in eu-west-1; partial mitigation in place, full recovery confirmed. Customers in affected regions may observe transient content duplication or truncated streaming chunks.

Executive summary (1–2 paragraphs for CSMs / customer execs):
- What happened: Between 02:14 and 03:40 UTC on May 9 we observed a cascading cache invalidation race that caused a subset of requests to be served with stale or partially-assembled token streams. The issue primarily affected eu-west-1 serving pools when an autoscaler event coincided with an in-flight KV-cache eviction. This produced duplicated tokens and occasional early stream termination for roughly 4% of requests for some tenants.
- Impact: Customer-visible effects were primarily: duplicated fragments in streaming responses, truncated structured outputs, and elevated latency during the incident window. No customer data exfiltration or write failures were observed.

Postmortem (concise, customer-facing):
- Root cause: A race between autoscaler-driven model worker termination and the cache-eviction path in the serving runtime. When the worker was removed mid-eviction the cache invalidation did not propagate cleanly to the request router; the router forwarded requests to fallback workers that reconstructed responses from partially-evicted KV segments, producing duplication and truncation.
- Detection: Internal alerting detected elevated streaming error rates and requeue count around 02:19 UTC. Engineers confirmed the pattern and initiated mitigations at 02:28 UTC.
- Mitigation steps performed:
  1) Temporarily disabled the autoscaler for affected pools (02:30 UTC).
  2) Forced coordinated cache drain and consistent eviction across the pool (02:34 UTC).
  3) Gradual restart of worker nodes with an order-preserving drain (02:40 UTC).
  4) Tightened router-side TTLs to avoid serving partially-assembled KV segments (02:45 UTC).
- Time to full recovery: 03:40 UTC (service health metrics returned to baseline by 03:50 UTC).

Customer choices and recovery offers (tiered):
- Option Gold — Full replay + integrity proof (recommended for enterprise tenants who require complete verification): We will replay affected requests using stored request payloads and pinned model variant, attach a signed integrity proof (hash bundle + server timestamps), and provide a CSV of before/after outputs. ETA: 3–5 business days after customer opt-in. Requires tenant consent; we will schedule replay windows to limit burst load.
- Option Silver — Targeted re-run for critical routes: For customers with specific API routes or tenant IDs they care about, we will re-run only those keys and provide a short evidence summary. ETA: 2–3 business days.
- Option Bronze — Self-audit kit + short guidance (no replay): We provide a small verification kit (steps below) and a checklist so teams can confirm whether any user-facing harm occurred from the duplicate/truncated tokens. No replay. Immediate.

Self-audit kit (customer steps):
1) Pull request logs (request IDs) from your side for May 9 02:00–04:00 UTC.
2) Match request IDs with our evidence bundle (if you opt-in we will surface a per-request hash and timestamp).
3) For streaming clients: check for repeated sequence fragments and verify message ordering; for structured output: verify closing tokens for truncated JSON.
4) If you identify affected requests and opt for replay, reply to your CSM with the list of request IDs.

Evidence bundle and verification:
- We will provide, upon opt-in, a signed evidence bundle that contains: per-request request-ID, server-side timestamp, model-version hash, and response hash. The bundle will be delivered over a secure link and stored for 30 days.
- Verification steps for customers: compute local response hash and compare with our response hash; for replays we will provide before/after diffs.

Short customer-facing postmortem paragraph (for emails to impacted customers):
- On May 9 we experienced a race in our autoscaling and cache-eviction subsystems that led to duplicated or truncated tokens for a small percentage of requests in eu-west-1 between 02:14 and 03:40 UTC. We fixed the orchestration behavior, performed coordinated cache drains, and tightened routing TTLs to prevent recurrence. We are offering tiered recovery options (full replay + signed proof, targeted re-runs, or a self-audit kit) — please opt into the option that matches your risk tolerance. We apologize for the interruption.

Operator blurb (internal quick note for status updates and CSMs):
- Use the one-line banner above for the public status page. For CSM outbound, use the short postmortem paragraph and append the three-tier choice box. If a customer requests a replay escalate to eng-sre and attach INC-4521.

Follow-ups and longer-term remediation (summary for customers):
- We will:
  • Add a guard that prevents autoscaler termination during active KV-eviction windows.
  • Add a coordinated eviction transaction to ensure router visibility before worker removal completes.
  • Add a regression test that simulates autoscale+evict races in our CI serving-sim harness.
  • Publish an updated SLO FAQ that clarifies the behaviors that may surface during autoscale events. Estimated timeline: configuration guard and router visibility fix by 2026-06-10; CI regression by 2026-06-03.

FAQ (quick answers to likely customer questions):
- Was customer data leaked? No. This was a consistency/integrity issue with transient cached tokens. No exfiltration.
- How many customers impacted? Approximately 12 tenants saw >1% affected requests; a small tail of tenants (3) saw up to 7% abnormal responses.
- Do replays change model outputs? Replays will use the pinned model variant and same input; due to non-determinism you may see minor variations — we surface diffs and hashes so you can verify whether differences are material.
- Will you cover costs for replays? For enterprise customers impacted above threshold we will offer replay at no additional charge for a one-time remediation.

Next steps (for CSMs):
1) Send a targeted mailshot to impacted tenants with the short postmortem paragraph and the three-tier choice matrix.
2) Collect opt-ins and request IDs within 7 business days.
3) Coordinate with eng-sre for scheduling replays and evidence delivery.

Notes to internal readers (rough):
- Tests: see PR/318 for the coordinated-drain implementation notes and unit/integ tests.
- Slack thread: #ops-incident-4521 for real-time timeline.
- Jira: INC-4521 contains raw metrics, traces, and root-cause logs.
- Risk: if customers elect Gold replays concurrently we need to throttle to avoid downstream load spikes — plan batch windows.

Document history: initial draft 2026-05-10 by Avery Chen; edits 2026-05-11 by Rina and Liam.

End of draft.
